newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Colombia tops Latin America murder league - paper.
newsitem.headline: Colombia tops Latin America murder league - paper.

text.p: Colombia has the highest murder rate in Latin America, followed by Jamaica and Brazil, Jornal do Brasil, quoting a World Bank report, said on Saturday.
It said Colombia's annual murder rate at the start of the 1990s was 89.5 per 100,000 inhabitants, followed by Jamaica at 70 per 100,000 and Brazil at 19.7 per 100,000.
Mexico, Venezuela, Trinidad and Tobago and Peru all had murder rates of between 11 and 18 per 100,000 inhabitants.
The lowest murder rates in the region were in Chile, Paraguay, Costa Rica, Uruguay and Argentina.
The newspaper said the World Bank report would be issued at a conference on urban violence in Rio de Janeiro this week.
Latin America on average had the highest incidence of murders in the world at 20 per 100,000 inhabitants, almost double that of 10.1 murders in the United States, the newspaper said.
The study said urban growth, bad wealth distribution and the dismantling of state social services were major factors which contributed to the higher violence rates.

In a related development, local newspapers on Saturday said police had found the bodies of five men shot and killed in a Rio de Janeiro slum in what appeared to be a battle between warring drug gangs.
Three other bodies, also believed to be murdered, were found on Friday in another shanty-town in the city, newspapers said.

Last month five youths were dragged off a bus and shot in the head, reportedly because they did not pay their fare. Police have arrested a security guard employed by the bus company in connection with the shootings.
